## Purpose

Use `beaver machine reboot` when a machine needs a full restart — after a kernel update, to
clear a wedged system service, or as a troubleshooting step your provider's support asked
for. Every container running on the machine goes down for the duration of the reboot and
comes back once the machine finishes booting.

Before rebooting, run `beaver machine reboot-impact` to see exactly what would be
interrupted — this is the safest way to confirm you're not about to take down something you
didn't expect.

## Syntax

```bash
beaver machine reboot <machine-id> [flags]
```

| Argument | Required | Accepted values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<machine-id>` | Yes | A machine ID or name from `beaver machine list`. |

## Flags

<ParamField query="--yes" type="boolean" default="false">
  Skip the confirmation prompt and reboot immediately. Without it, you'll be asked to
  confirm before anything happens. See [shared flags](/cli/shared-flags#yes) — no
  command-specific interaction here.
</ParamField>

## Consequences

Rebooting a machine takes down **every container running on it** — not just one
application — for the duration of the reboot. There is no partial or rolling reboot at the
machine level. The command returns once the reboot request is accepted; it does not wait for
the machine to finish coming back up.

<Warning>
  This affects every container on the machine, not just one project. Run `beaver machine
  reboot-impact <machine-id>` first to see the full list of what will be interrupted.
</Warning>

The action itself isn't reversible (you can't "un-reboot"), but it's a normal, expected
machine operation — the risk is scope (everything on the machine), not permanence.

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash Check impact first
beaver machine reboot-impact srv_web01
```

```bash Reboot with confirmation
beaver machine reboot srv_web01
```

```bash Reboot without prompting (e.g. in a script)
beaver machine reboot srv_web01 --yes
```

</CodeGroup>

**Expected output** (reviewed against source, not executed against a live machine):

```text
✓ Done
```

## Results & failures

| Situation | What you'll see | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Success | `✓ Done` | The reboot request was accepted; the machine is restarting. |
| Confirmation declined | Command exits without rebooting | Re-run with confirmation, or add `--yes` once you're sure. |
| `failed to reboot machine: ...` | An error naming the underlying failure | The machine may be unreachable or already mid-operation; check `beaver machine overview <machine-id>`. |
